Script:


Time code Description / Visual
00: 00 Report Card In 2015 the Gauteng Department of Health announced they were terminating the contract with life Esidimeni and that over 1700 state psychiatric patients would be moved to NGO’s. They were repeatedly warned by various specialists that these NGO were ill equipped. And that the department was not ready for this move. But the then MEC Qedani Mahlangu ignored all the warning
00:26 Devi interview with Qedani Devi: SASOP, SADAG AND Section 27 these are the exact issues that they were trying to raise with the department
MEC: but I don’t know how you pre-empt issues and then worry…
Devi: because you can see it coming.
MEC: okay, unless they were foretellers
00:39 Voice over In September 2016 we broke the story that some of state psychiatric patients that had been moved from Life Esidimeni had in fact passed away. One of the first deaths that we confirmed was that of Christine Nxule sister Virginia who passed away under mysterious circumstances at an NGO called Precious Angle care.
01:01 Christine They need to be charged, the MEC needs to be charged. This is for me this is murder its just simple murder
: Voice over We followed the story for a year as the death toll continued to rise. Today he death toll is sitting at over 120 more that 120 lives that could’ve been saved had the government just done better if they had just listened.
Soon after our interview MEC Qedani Mahlangu promptly resigned and the ombudsman was requested by the national health minister to put together a report to what happened and to make a recommendation ion how to move forward. It is now 120 days since the report was released. One of the Ombudsman’s recommendations was that all the NGO where people died be shut down and investigated but Mosego house where Freddy Collet passed away from starvation and dehydration is still open. MEC Gwen Rabogana took over from MEC Qedani Mahlangu for the Gauteng department of health
02:02 Interview with Gwen MEC: There are 11 of the 27 NGO that are still running

Devi: and Mosego house? Are they still opened?

MEC: that matter is with the police, my understand is that there is likely to be an inquest on each on the deaths but those are the processes that are going through the south African police
02:22 Voice over And precious angle care where Christine’s sister victoria passed away may have been closed down but Christine still gas not received her sisters post mortem. In fact almost all of the families who lost loved ones are still waiting to find out what happened to them. The SAPS HAS Begun their investigations though by interviewing all the families. Investigations can take time but at least they have started so here you get a C

The most urgent recommendation was that all patients still in NGO be moved to a place of safety
02:58 MEC Gwen MEC: what we have on our records was that there were 1012 patients that left life Esidimeni. 820 patients those were relocated in the first phase, which started, from march to may. There are those patients about 300 or so that were discharged to home. There are patients there are those I think the number is around 60 that we are still trying to verify where they are.


03:27 Voice over Most of the patients are now safe but 60 people are now missing and that’s simply not good enough. So here you get an E.

The one person who is unarguably accountable for this tragedy is the former MEC for heath Qedani Mahlangu. But she resigned without taking any responsibility.
03:48 Devi: what happens to the former MEC is there going to be any legal action and who will have to decide that?

MEC: that has not been an area of focus actually our focus is to restore the reputation of the department through making sure that we you know assist the patients to be in a more secure environment
04:08 Voice over The fact that Qedani Mahlangu has not been held accountable its simply unacceptable and a pattern which is continuing with MEC across the country so here you get an F
With regards to the other staff the ombudsman made special recommendation for both Dr. Manamela the director for the department of health and Dr. Slovene the head of department
04:29 Devi: Dr. Manamela she was the person in fact issued those illegal licenses to the NGOs at the first place. Now the Ombudsman recommended disciplinary proceedings for gross misconduct and what has happened since then?

MEC: Dr. Manamela was suspended is on suspension to be taken through to disciplinary action we know that she is one of those who appealed to the minister through the appease process
04:55 Voice over Basically It’s been 120 days since the report came out and still no one has been held accountable. In fact both Dr. Manamela and Dr. Slovene are on paid suspension and has costed the taxpayer over R1 million so far. Six other officials who were hands on during this Esidimeni move are still working for the Gauteng Department of health here you get an F.
05:21 Devi: the former MEC kept saying to us over and over again that the main reason was we needed to save money, we need to save costs, but I think we can accept now, as fact is the fact that it cost us a lot more money.

MEC: indeed, it didn’t cost us even much money than more it costs lives. It was very costly
05:41 Voice over The mistakes made here by the Gauteng department of health seemed to be slowly getting fixed but again it is taking too long and not all the patients are safely relocated so as a whole we give you an F but what this tragedy has done is shine a light on mental health at large so hopefully this wont happen again.
